sections.title: Habit and origin
sections.text: Quinoa is an Andean annual in the Amaranthaceae, not a grass cereal. Its height varies greatly with cultivar and growing conditions, from about 20 cm to 3 m. Angular stems bear variable alternate leaves and dense panicles; the crop is now grown in many regions.

sections.title: Seeds and food
sections.text: Its seeds are eaten as a grain and the leaves can also be used as a vegetable. Seed coats of some varieties contain bitter saponins, so food preparation depends on the variety and suitable washing or processing. The plate shows a colourful cultivar, but that colour is not constant across the species.
